title: FactorLedger: Effector Interaction Ledgers for Closed-Loop VLA Correction
hook: The arm with the larger isolated effect need not be the arm that should be edited: in bimanual contact, a coupled action correction can raise RoboTwin task success while the corresponding single-effector correction lowers it. FactorLedger tests and exploits that reversal instead of treating a proposal-conditioned future as one indivisible feedback signal.
hook_shape_rationale: Shape (a), surprising empirical reveal: the named downstream metric is RoboTwin task success, and the predicted direction reverses between a marginal-only edit and an interaction-aware joint edit under the same frozen checkpoint. Shape (c) was considered but rejected because FactorLedger spends additional FastWAM rollouts and therefore cannot honestly claim to be no larger on inference compute.

gap_closure.how_closed: Corpus support is thin for robot VLA, so the structurally closest C25 move is used: the VLA emits one joint proposal, a typed marginal–interaction ledger becomes the machine-checkable handoff, and OSQP returns a box-constrained channel-scale correction that is verified by a second FastWAM rollout before execution.

gap_closure.how_closed: Corpus support is thin for continuous bimanual VLA interventions, so C02 is instantiated as state- and checkpoint-matched fractional-factorial perturbations whose independent oracle is RoboTwin's executed task-success predicate; their degree-two response projection separates per-channel marginals from left–right non-additivity.

core_mechanism: At control state o_t (the current RGB frames, proprioception, and language goal), a frozen OpenPI π0.5 checkpoint proposes its native action chunk a^0, and the checkpoint's published action schema defines a set G of effector–channel groups, one temporal trajectory per native left- or right-effector coordinate. Let h be the proprioceptive hold-action chunk and let α_g scale group g between h_g and a^0_g, so a(α)_g = h_g + α_g(a^0_g-h_g) and the unmodified proposal is α = 1. A randomized D-optimal signed design Z produces local variants α^(b) = 1 + εz^(b); ε defaults to the held-out RoboTwin rank-calibration minimizer, and B defaults to the largest design that fits the measured E0 FastWAM rollout budget. FastWAM F_ψ receives the same o_t, language goal, stochastic seed ξ, and each a(α^(b)); a calibrated logistic outcome head q_φ, fitted from existing RoboTwin simulator success labels on frozen FastWAM rollout features, maps each predicted rollout to a success probability y_b. Weighted hierarchical regression fits y_b = β_0 + Σ_g m_g α_g^(b) + Σ_{g<h} I_gh α_g^(b)α_h^(b) + e_b; λ_m and λ_I default to their nested held-out calibration minimizers, and the typed ledger L_t = {G, ε, B, Z, m, I, covariance, calibration provenance} is computable without model gradients. The precise local estimand is the degree-two design-weighted L2 projection of q_φ(F_ψ(o_t,a(1+εZ),ξ)) over the randomized local intervention design and FastWAM seed distribution, conditional on o_t and a^0; m_g is its marginal coefficient and I_gh its non-additive coefficient, not a Shapley allocation or a global causal effect. The anchor leg delegates L_t to OSQP: at α = 1 it forms d_g = m_g + Σ_{h≠g}I_gh, then solves a quadratic update with positive correction weight λ_c under the native action box and -r ≤ α_g-1 ≤ r; λ_c and r default to their joint held-out simulator calibration choice, yielding α*. A second common-seed FastWAM rollout verifies q_φ(F_ψ(o_t,a(α*),ξ)) against the unmodified proposal; the corrected chunk is executed only when its predicted score is higher, otherwise a^0 is retained. This sequential diagnostic-to-solver handoff makes the interaction ledger load-bearing during action construction, while the raw m and I remain auditable against executed matched-state RoboTwin interventions.
core_mechanism_reasoning:
BLOCK 1 — PREMISES ledger:
P1. Within calibrated ε and r, FastWAM preserves the ordering of nearby action variants under RoboTwin success; holding state, checkpoint, horizon, and seed fixed makes this plausible, but it is untested — falsification target through the fitted interaction matrix I.
P2. The native OpenPI action schema supplies a stable partition G because RoboTwin and the checkpoint explicitly expose left/right action coordinates rather than learned role labels.
P3. A degree-two response is adequate for one local correction even when global dynamics are higher order; this empirical premise restricts all claims to the calibrated neighborhood and executed E0 states.
P4. Logistic q_φ ranks FastWAM rollouts for the selected RoboTwin tasks; it is fitted from RoboTwin's existing simulator success predicate and calibrated on held-out tasks and states, not from VLA self-judgment.
OBSERVATION-MODEL premise. States come from frozen π0.5 RoboTwin rollouts, design rows are randomized independently of outcomes, and the FastWAM seed is coupled across variants. Design-score averages target the FastWAM-seed expectation without outcome-conditioned selection, but penalized m and I are not claimed unbiased; policy occupancy, off-support perturbations, regularization, FastWAM error, and q_φ error also bar an unrestricted real-dynamics claim.
ESTIMAND. For fixed (o_t,a^0), the target is the main and pairwise coefficients of the degree-two design-weighted L2 projection of predicted RoboTwin success over α=1+εZ and ξ; E0 separately tests whether each I_gh preserves the sign of the executed-simulator mixed contrast.
BLOCK 2 — NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT: The runnable naive anchor scores one left-only and one right-only FastWAM perturbation, edits the larger marginal, and ignores paired perturbations. Branch (i): it silently assumes additive effector responses, which fails in closed-chain contact and role-switching phases; FactorLedger confronts that failure by estimating I from joint interventions and letting I change the downstream action update. Factorial contrasts, response-surface regression, and QP are standard tools, but VLA chunks are temporally coupled, probes can leave policy support, the response is WAM-observed, and the ledger must be estimated and consumed inside one bounded correction; common-seed pairing, simulator calibration, typed handoff, and online verification are the domain-specific contribution.
BLOCK 3 — Design rationale: The gaps form a sequential pipeline: without the ledger the solver has no responsibility signal, and without the solver the ledger is only post-hoc. COMA credit, Shapley averaging, fixed leader–follower roles, and unconstrained neural refinement were rejected because they revisit occupied lineage nodes or lack a checkable mixed response. Cross-run negatives are separated explicitly: there is no feasibility-flip boundary score (CBSM), geometry–action crossover (GISS-2x2), censoring replay (ExitReplay), or fixed-scaffold regret with a reset-clone oracle (ScaffoldFracture); only effector action channels around one frozen proposal are perturbed, and the ledger drives a constrained corrector.
core_mechanism_steps:
1. Freeze the existing OpenPI π0.5 policy and FastWAM checkpoints; on RoboTwin, record frozen-policy states, native action chunks, FastWAM rollout features, and the simulator's existing task-success label, then fit and calibrate q_φ on disjoint task/state splits. Inputs: RGB, proprioception, language goals, action chunks, simulator labels; output: a frozen outcome head with held-out calibration records.
2. Parse the OpenPI action schema into G, where each group is one named left- or right-effector channel across the native chunk horizon H; set H by the checkpoint's native action-chunk definition and construct the proprioceptive hold chunk h. Inputs: schema, a^0, current proprioception; outputs: G, h, and the affine action map a(α).
3. Select ε on held-out RoboTwin states by minimizing rank disagreement between FastWAM-scored and executed action variants, and set B to the largest D-optimal signed design that fits the measured E0 rollout latency and memory budget. Inputs: calibration states and hardware measurements; outputs: named ε, B, and design Z with its provenance.
4. For every row z^(b), build a(1+εz^(b)), reuse one FastWAM seed ξ across the matched variants, and compute y_b = q_φ(F_ψ(o_t,a(1+εz^(b)),ξ)). Inputs: o_t, a^0, h, Z, ε, F_ψ, q_φ; outputs: a matched score vector y and cached rollout features.
5. Fit the hierarchical degree-two response using λ_m and λ_I chosen by nested held-out calibration, and serialize L_t = {G, ε, Z, m, I, covariance, calibration provenance}; reject no rows post-outcome. Inputs: Z and y; output: a schema-validated marginal–interaction ledger.
6. At α = 1, compute d_g = m_g + Σ_{h≠g}I_gh and call OSQP on max_Δ d^TΔ - (λ_c/2)||Δ||_2^2 subject to the native action box and -r ≤ Δ_g ≤ r, where λ_c and r are selected on held-out simulator states. Inputs: L_t and action bounds; outputs: Δ* and α* = 1+Δ*, with solver status and residuals written back to L_t.
7. Run FastWAM once more on a(α*) with the coupled seed; if its q_φ score exceeds that of a^0, pass the corrected chunk to the policy execution path, otherwise pass a^0. Inputs: proposed and corrected chunks; output: the actually executed chunk plus a machine-checkable accept/retain verdict.
8. In E0, restore identical RoboTwin states and seeds to execute a^0, the naive marginal-only correction, FactorLedger, and the interaction-pairing negative control; log task success, intervention latency, m, I, predicted gains, and executed gains. Inputs: saved simulator states and four correction arms; output: paired downstream outcomes and a sign-calibration audit of I.
falsification_prediction: On existing RoboTwin bimanual contact tasks, use one frozen OpenPI π0.5 checkpoint and one frozen FastWAM checkpoint, restore identical simulator states and seeds, and compare the unmodified action chunk, the runnable marginal-only corrector, and FactorLedger while measuring RoboTwin task success and correction latency. If the mechanism works, task success increases for FactorLedger relative to both the frozen proposal and the marginal-only corrector, especially on states where the ledger predicts that a joint edit and the largest-marginal single-effector edit have opposite downstream ordering. The single load-bearing variable is the fitted left–right interaction matrix I: as a negative control, independently permute the right-effector design rows before fitting I while leaving the marginal columns, outcome head, rollout count, and solver unchanged. This destroys matched non-additivity without deleting marginal information; the prediction is that downstream RoboTwin task success returns toward the marginal-only/frozen-policy baseline rather than merely making entries of I small.
compute_budget: 12 A100-40GB GPU-days (approximately 6 80GB-class GPU-days) for outcome-head fitting, FastWAM factorial rollouts, calibration, and paired RoboTwin E0 evaluation; $0 paid API for the full campaign. This is comfortable within the stated four-A100, rollback-first envelope, and B is selected from measured local rollout capacity rather than assumed throughput.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: CoCo measures and trains whole-action counterfactual consistency, whereas FactorLedger constructs a local effector–channel response surface with explicit marginal and mixed coefficients and uses those coefficients to change the next action chunk.

ω-EVA feeds one proposal-conditioned latent future into a tri-branch neural refiner, whereas FactorLedger emits a typed marginal–interaction ledger from matched action interventions and delegates its correction to a constrained solver with an inspectable responsibility boundary.

ManiGaussian++ fixes acting and stabilizing roles in its hierarchy, whereas FactorLedger estimates state-local left–right interaction coefficients without assigning either arm a persistent role and permits the correction responsibility to reverse by state.

The optimizer interaction calculus identifies Boolean effects for declared optimizer response classes, whereas FactorLedger defines a policy-occupancy-conditional continuous action-chunk estimand, calibrates it through a learned world model against executed simulator outcomes, and makes it operational in closed-loop VLA correction.

what_step_was_missed: ω-EVA would have needed to replace its indivisible proposal-conditioned-future feedback with matched left/right action-channel interventions, fit their marginal and mixed success-response coefficients into a typed ledger, and make that ledger the input to the action-update solver.
